scope: Theorem 18.6 (Uniform curvature of the true cap potentials) of the manuscript “Critical mixing in the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model” (preprints/Critical-mixing-in-the-Sherrington-Kirkpatrick-model-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 227 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 3ac6296cc238bae9), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 170. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a finite field radius L0. There is C = C(L0) < ∞ such that for every ϵ > 0 there are constants ptop > 0 and s0 > 0 for which, with probability tending to one, the following assertions hold simultaneously for every pmin(n) ≤ p ≤ ptop, pmin(n) = (√ log n n )1/3 . For all h ∈ Pp with |αp(h)| ≤ s0p2, Pp∇2 ϕp(h)Pp ⪯ 1 + ϵ p2 Pp. (18.21) For all h ∈ Pp with ∥h∥ ≤ L0p2Mp, Pp∇2 ϕp(h)Pp ⪯ C p2 Pp. (18.22) The constants are independent of n, p, h. The field radius and all coarse constants may be fixed before the sharp curvature tolerances. The lower endpoint pmin(n) may be changed by a fixed factor.
